scope: Leviticus 26–27, all 80 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 26–27. The exact original XML records include all three annotations at 26:7, 26:8 and 26:28; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four prohibited objects and selects on it for the stone’s preposition; a note preserves the uncertain installation and before-it alternative.
verses.before: “You will not make idols for yourselves, nor set up a carved image or a pillar for yourselves, nor place a figured stone in your land to bow down to it, for I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: “Do not make idols for yourselves. Do not set up a carved image or a sacred pillar, or place a figured stone in your land to bow down on it. I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not make idols for yourselves, nor set up a carved image or a pillar for yourselves, nor place a figured stone in your land to bow down to it, for I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves Sabbath and sanctuary as paired obligations and retains the divine identity refrain.
verses.before: You will keep my Sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Keep my Sabbaths and hold my sanctuary in reverence. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep my Sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains walking as the opening conduct image and lets the condition continue across the verse label to its result.
verses.before: If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments and do them,
verses.after: If you walk by my statutes and keep my commandments by doing them,
verses.tsw_comparator: If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments and do them,

verses.rationale: Makes rain, crops and tree fruit three clear elements while retaining divine agency and seasonal timing.
verses.before: I will give your rains in their season, the land will give its produce, and the trees of the field will give their fruit.
verses.after: I will give you rain in its season. The land will yield its crops, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give your rains in their season, the land will give its produce, and the trees of the field will give their fruit.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the overlapping agricultural seasons without replacing them with generic prosperity; bread and security establish later reversals.
verses.before: Your threshing will reach to the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will reach to the sowing. You will eat your bread to the full and dwell securely in your land.
verses.after: Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until sowing time. You will eat your fill of bread and live securely in your land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your threshing will reach to the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will reach to the sowing. You will eat your bread to the full and dwell securely in your land.

verses.rationale: Keeps peace, unafraid rest, harmful animals and sword distinct; preserves the sword image rather than substituting a modern military term.
verses.before: I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one making you afraid. I will remove harmful animals from the land, and the sword will not pass through your land.
verses.after: I will give peace in the land. You will lie down with no one to frighten you. I will rid the land of harmful animals, and no sword will pass through your land.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one making you afraid. I will remove harmful animals from the land, and the sword will not pass through your land.

verses.rationale: Retains the already clear wording, including pursuit, actual violent defeat and the sword language repeated in the next verse; no change is needed merely to differ from TSW.
verses.before: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
verses.after: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.

verses.rationale: Keeps both asymmetric numerical ratios and the repeated sword result without rationalizing the arithmetic.
verses.before: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
verses.after: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.

verses.rationale: Retains turn-toward, fruitful and multiply language while clarifying population growth and continuing covenant commitment.
verses.before: I will turn toward you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish my covenant with you.
verses.after: I will turn toward you, make you fruitful and increase your numbers. I will uphold my covenant with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will turn toward you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish my covenant with you.

verses.rationale: Makes the old/new sequence readable and preserves abundance beyond a single harvest.
verses.before: You will eat old produce long stored, and you will clear out the old because of the new.
verses.after: You will still be eating old, stored grain when you have to clear it out to make room for the new.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will eat old produce long stored, and you will clear out the old because of the new.

verses.rationale: Keeps the dwelling image and strong abhorrence verb, anticipating its reversal in verse 30 rather than weakening it to dislike.
verses.before: I will set my dwelling place among you, and I will not reject you.
verses.after: I will place my dwelling among you, and I will not abhor you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will set my dwelling place among you, and I will not reject you.

verses.rationale: Retains walking and the two reciprocal covenant declarations in sentences suited to reading aloud.
verses.before: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
verses.after: I will walk among you. I will be your God, and you will be my people.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.

verses.rationale: Preserves slavery, broken yoke bars and bodily upright walking rather than replacing the ancient image with an abstract freedom slogan.
verses.before: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
verses.after: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt so you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.

verses.rationale: Begins the counter-condition with listen and all, retaining its continuation across verses 15–16.
verses.before: But if you will not listen to me and will not do all these commandments,
verses.after: But if you will not listen to me or carry out all these commandments,
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you will not listen to me and will not do all these commandments,

verses.rationale: Keeps rejection, abhorrence, refusal and covenant-breaking as connected actions rather than a vague failure to obey.
verses.before: if you reject my statutes and if you abhor my ordinances, so that you do not do all my commandments and so break my covenant,
verses.after: if you reject my statutes and abhor my ordinances, refusing to do all my commandments and breaking my covenant,
verses.tsw_comparator: if you reject my statutes and if you abhor my ordinances, so that you do not do all my commandments and so break my covenant,

verses.rationale: Preserves divine agency, both illness terms and bodily images without assigning a modern diagnosis; crop clarifies what enemies eat.
verses.before: then I will do this to you: I will appoint sudden terror over you, wasting disease and fever that consume the eyes and make life waste away. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.
verses.after: then I, in turn, will do this to you: I will bring terror on you, wasting disease and fever that wear out your eyes and drain your life. You will sow your seed for nothing; your enemies will eat the crop.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will do this to you: I will appoint sudden terror over you, wasting disease and fever that consume the eyes and make life waste away. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.

verses.rationale: Keeps face-against as the reversal of turning toward, names hostile rule and retains the no-pursuer fear pattern.
verses.before: I will set my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. People who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one pursues you.
verses.after: I will set my face against you. You will be defeated by your enemies, those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee though no one pursues you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will set my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one pursues you.

verses.rationale: Retains the renewed conditional stage, disciplinary verb and exact sevenfold escalation.
verses.before: If after all this you still will not listen to me, I will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.after: If you still will not listen to me after all this, I will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: If after all this you still will not listen to me, I will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.

verses.rationale: Clarifies pride-of-strength while retaining both metal images instead of replacing them with drought alone.
verses.before: I will break the pride of your strength. I will make your heavens like iron and your land like bronze.
verses.after: I will break the pride you take in your strength. I will make your sky like iron and your land like bronze.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will break the pride of your strength. I will make your heavens like iron and your land like bronze.

verses.rationale: Preserves wasted effort and both crop failures as direct reversals of verse 4.
verses.before: Your strength will be spent in vain, for your land will not give its produce, and the trees of the land will not give their fruit.
verses.after: You will spend your strength for nothing. Your land will yield no crops, and its trees will bear no fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your strength will be spent in vain, for your land will not give its produce, and the trees of the land will not give their fruit.

verses.rationale: Uses hostility provisionally for qeri and retains walking, refusal and sevenfold blows; a note identifies the rare word’s uncertainty.
verses.before: If you walk in opposition to me and will not listen to me, I will multiply your blows sevenfold according to your sins.
verses.after: If you walk in hostility toward me and refuse to listen, I will bring sevenfold blows on you for your sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you walk in opposition to me and will not listen to me, I will multiply your blows sevenfold according to your sins.

verses.rationale: Makes the bereavement verb’s human cost explicit and preserves livestock loss, population reduction and empty roads.
verses.before: I will send wild animals among you, and they will bereave you of children, destroy your livestock, and make you few, so that your roads become desolate.
verses.after: I will send wild animals among you. They will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock and reduce your numbers, leaving your roads deserted.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will send wild animals among you, and they will bereave you of children, destroy your livestock, and make you few, so that your roads become desolate.

verses.rationale: Retains the failure to accept correction and repeated hostile walking, linking the condition to verse 24.
verses.before: If through these things you will not be corrected by me but continue to walk in opposition to me,
verses.after: If you will not accept my correction even through these things, but keep walking in hostility toward me,
verses.tsw_comparator: If through these things you will not be corrected by me but continue to walk in opposition to me,

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal hostility, emphatic divine subject and another sevenfold stage.
verses.before: then I also will walk in opposition to you, and I myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.after: then I too will walk in hostility toward you. I myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I also will walk in opposition to you, and I myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant vengeance, city gathering, pestilence and enemy capture without flattening these into one generic punishment.
verses.before: I will bring a sword against you that executes the vengeance of the covenant. When you gather into your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you will be given into the hand of the enemy.
verses.after: I will bring a sword against you to avenge the covenant. When you gather in your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you will be handed over to an enemy.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring a sword against you that executes the vengeance of the covenant. When you gather into your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you will be given into the hand of the enemy.

verses.rationale: Retains staff-of-bread with a compact explanation, ten women, one oven and weighed rations; hunger reverses verse 5.
verses.before: When I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and return your bread by weight. You will eat but not be satisfied.
verses.after: When I break the staff of bread that sustains you, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and hand it back to you by weight. You will eat, but you will not be satisfied.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and return your bread by weight. You will eat but not be satisfied.

verses.rationale: Preserves the final renewed condition and the repeated conduct phrase without merging it with earlier stages.
verses.before: If in spite of this you will not listen to me but continue to walk in opposition to me,
verses.after: If you still will not listen to me through all this, but keep walking in hostility toward me,
verses.tsw_comparator: If in spite of this you will not listen to me but continue to walk in opposition to me,

verses.rationale: Retains the added fury and emphatic agent as the hostility sequence reaches its fourth sevenfold warning.
verses.before: then I will walk in furious opposition to you, and I myself will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.after: I will walk in furious hostility toward you. I myself will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will walk in furious opposition to you, and I myself will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit cannibalism, both sexes and repeated eating clause, without euphemizing the horror or adding circumstances absent from this verse.
verses.before: You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
verses.after: You will eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you will eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.

verses.rationale: Keeps disputed cult installation provisionally as incense altars, preserves corpse/corpse wordplay and the reversal of verse 11.
verses.before: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and place your corpses upon the corpses of your idols, and I will abhor you.
verses.after: I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars. I will pile your corpses on the corpses of your idols, and I will abhor you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and place your corpses upon the corpses of your idols, and I will abhor you.

verses.rationale: Retains plural sanctuaries and the sensory rejection of the recurrent offering-aroma formula.
verses.before: I will make your cities a ruin and your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not smell the pleasing aroma of your offerings.
verses.after: I will turn your cities into ruins and leave your sanctuaries desolate. I will not smell your pleasing aromas.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make your cities a ruin and your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not smell the pleasing aroma of your offerings.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic divine agency and the enemies’ reaction to the devastated land they inhabit.
verses.before: I myself will make the land desolate, and your enemies who settle in it will be appalled at it.
verses.after: I myself will make the land desolate. Even your enemies who settle there will be appalled by it.
verses.tsw_comparator: I myself will make the land desolate, and your enemies who settle in it will be appalled at it.

verses.rationale: Keeps dispersal, drawn sword and separate land/city consequences as the earlier pursuit promise is reversed.
verses.before: I will scatter you among the nations and draw out the sword after you. Your land will become a desolation, and your cities will become ruins.
verses.after: I will scatter you among the nations and draw a sword in pursuit of you. Your land will be desolate and your cities ruined.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will scatter you among the nations and draw out the sword after you. Your land will become a desolation, and your cities will become ruins.

verses.rationale: Retains both Sabbath-enjoyment clauses and the land as subject; note preserves making-up-for-rest as another sense of ratsah.
verses.before: Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
verses.after: Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths throughout the time it lies desolate, while you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.

verses.rationale: Makes missed land rest explicit while retaining the contrast between desolation and earlier habitation.
verses.before: All the days it lies desolate it will have the rest it did not have during your Sabbaths when you lived upon it.
verses.after: All the time it lies desolate, it will have the rest it did not have on your Sabbaths when you lived on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the days it lies desolate it will have the rest it did not have during your Sabbaths when you lived upon it.

verses.rationale: Keeps survivors, inward fear, the slight leaf sound and the repeated no-pursuer paradox without converting dread into a modern psychiatric diagnosis.
verses.before: As for those of you who remain, I will bring faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a windblown leaf will pursue them. They will flee as one flees from the sword, and they will fall when no one pursues.
verses.after: As for those of you who survive, I will fill their hearts with dread in their enemies’ lands. The sound of a windblown leaf will drive them to flight. They will run as though fleeing a sword and fall though no one pursues them.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for those of you who remain, I will bring faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a windblown leaf will pursue them. They will flee as one flees from the sword, and they will fall when no one pursues.

verses.rationale: Preserves stumbling and absent pursuit; stand is selected for the rare tequmah, with possible absence of a defender noted.
verses.before: They will stumble over one another as if fleeing before the sword, though no one pursues. You will have no strength to stand before your enemies.
verses.after: They will stumble over one another as though fleeing a sword, though no one pursues them. You will have no strength to stand against your enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will stumble over one another as though fleeing before the sword, though no one pursues. You will have no strength to stand before your enemies.

verses.rationale: Retains the land’s devouring image rather than replacing it with a generalized exile statement.
verses.before: You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.
verses.after: You will perish among the nations. Your enemies’ land will devour you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.

verses.rationale: Keeps both wasting clauses and intergenerational guilt; the compressed with-them relationship is made intelligible without shifting blame solely to ancestors.
verses.before: Those of you who remain will waste away in their guilt in the lands of your enemies, and because of the guilt of their ancestors with them they will waste away.
verses.after: Those of you who survive will waste away in your enemies’ lands because of their guilt. They will also waste away because of their ancestors’ guilt along with their own.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those of you who remain will waste away in their guilt in the lands of your enemies, and because of the guilt of their ancestors with them they will waste away.

verses.rationale: Selects a declarative continuation rather than inserting if; preserves confession of both generations and repeated hostility, with conditional alternative noted.
verses.before: But if they confess their guilt and the guilt of their ancestors—their unfaithfulness by which they acted unfaithfully against me, and also that they walked in opposition to me,
verses.after: They will confess their guilt and their ancestors’ guilt—their unfaithfulness in betraying me and their walking in hostility toward me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they confess their guilt and the guilt of their ancestors—their unfaithfulness by which they acted unfaithfully against me, and also that they walked in opposition to me,

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal hostility and the uncircumcised-heart image; then perhaps represents uncertain o az, with alternatives noted alongside ratsah’s penalty sense.
verses.before: so that I also walked in opposition to them and brought them into the land of their enemies—if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they accept the punishment of their guilt,
verses.after: I too will walk in hostility toward them and bring them into their enemies’ land. Then perhaps their uncircumcised heart will be humbled, and they will bear the penalty for their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that I also walked in opposition to them and brought them into the land of their enemies—if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they accept the punishment of their guilt,

verses.rationale: Preserves reverse ancestral order, three covenant mentions and three acts of remembering rather than compressing the promise.
verses.before: then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and I will also remember my covenant with Isaac and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.
verses.after: I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac; I will remember my covenant with Abraham. And I will remember the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and I will also remember my covenant with Isaac and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps land rest and guilt-payment connected through the repeated Hebrew root, and renders the doubled causal phrase emphatically.
verses.before: The land will be abandoned by them and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them. They will accept the punishment of their guilt because they rejected my ordinances and abhorred my statutes.
verses.after: The land will be abandoned by them and enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them. They will bear the penalty for their guilt, precisely because they rejected my ordinances and abhorred my statutes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The land will be abandoned by them and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them. They will accept the punishment of their guilt because they rejected my ordinances and abhorred my statutes.

verses.rationale: Retains the limit on rejection and destruction rather than contradicting verse 30 with an unqualified claim of no abhorrence.
verses.before: Yet even then, while they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them completely and break my covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.
verses.after: Yet even then, when they are in their enemies’ land, I will not reject or abhor them so completely that I destroy them and break my covenant with them. I am the LORD their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet even then, while they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them completely and break my covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.

verses.rationale: Preserves remembrance for the descendants, exodus ancestors, public witness of nations and the stated purpose of divine relationship.
verses.before: For their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations so that I might be their God. I am the LORD.”
verses.after: For their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of Egypt in the sight of the nations to be their God. I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations so that I might be their God. I am the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Retains all three legal categories, covenant parties, Sinai and Moses’ mediation as the closing narrative statement.
verses.before: These are the statutes, ordinances, and instructions that the LORD established between the LORD and the Israelites on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
verses.after: These are the statutes, ordinances and instructions the LORD established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the statutes, ordinances, and instructions that the LORD established between the LORD and the Israelites on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves the new divine speech that introduces the final chapter’s valuation rules.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Unfolds the compressed persons-and-valuation clause without depicting the person as an ordinary animal offering; special vow is a noted lexical choice.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the valuation of a person,
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the assessed value of a person, use these amounts.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the valuation of a person,

verses.rationale: Keeps sex, both stated age endpoints, exact amount, silver and sanctuary standard without assigning a moral worth to the valuation.
verses.before: the valuation for a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old will be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.
verses.after: For a male from twenty to sixty years old, the assessed value is fifty shekels of silver, using the sanctuary shekel.
verses.tsw_comparator: the valuation for a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.

verses.rationale: Retains the female valuation in the same age band as verse 3 and the exact thirty-shekel amount.
verses.before: If the person is female, the valuation will be thirty shekels.
verses.after: For a female, the assessed value is thirty shekels.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the person is female, the valuation shall be thirty shekels.

verses.rationale: Makes the paired amounts easy to compare while retaining both sexes and stated age boundaries.
verses.before: If the person is from five years old up to twenty years old, the valuation for a male will be twenty shekels and for a female ten shekels.
verses.after: From five to twenty years old, assess a male at twenty shekels and a female at ten shekels.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the person is from five years old up to twenty years old, the valuation for a male shall be twenty shekels and for a female ten shekels.

verses.rationale: Preserves the one-month lower bound, five-year upper bound, both amounts and repeated silver designation.
verses.before: If the person is from one month old up to five years old, the valuation for a male will be five shekels of silver and for a female three shekels of silver.
verses.after: From one month to five years old, assess a male at five shekels of silver and a female at three shekels of silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the person is from one month old up to five years old, the valuation for a male shall be five shekels of silver and for a female three shekels of silver.

verses.rationale: Keeps the open upper age band and the fifteen/ten distinction without calculating modern equivalents.
verses.before: If the person is sixty years old or older, the valuation for a male will be fifteen shekels and for a female ten shekels.
verses.after: From sixty years old and upward, assess a male at fifteen shekels and a female at ten shekels.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the person is sixty years old or older, the valuation for a male shall be fifteen shekels and for a female ten shekels.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the person vowed from the person paying where the pronoun is compressed; preserves the priest’s assessment based on means, with referent uncertainty noted.
verses.before: But if someone is too poor to pay the valuation, that person will be presented before the priest, and the priest will assign a valuation according to what the one who made the vow can afford.
verses.after: If the person making the vow is too poor to pay the assessed value, have the person being valued stand before the priest. The priest is to set the amount according to what the one who made the vow can afford.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if someone is too poor to pay the valuation, that person shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall assign a valuation according to what the one who made the vow can afford.

verses.rationale: Keeps the eligible-animal condition and dedication’s holy status rather than implying every animal is suitable for sacrifice.
verses.before: If the vow concerns an animal that may be presented as an offering to the LORD, anything given from such animals to the LORD will be holy.
verses.after: If the vow concerns an animal of a kind that may be offered to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD becomes holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the vow concerns an animal that may be presented as an offering to the LORD, anything given from such animals to the LORD shall be holy.

verses.rationale: Retains both forbidden directions of exchange and the consequence for both animals, even where the substitute seems better.
verses.before: It will not be altered or exchanged, good for bad or bad for good. If one animal is exchanged for another, both the original animal and its substitute will be holy.
verses.after: Do not replace it or exchange it, good for bad or bad for good. If one animal is exchanged for another, both the original and its substitute become holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall not be altered or exchanged, good for bad or bad for good. If one animal is exchanged for another, both the original animal and its substitute shall be holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps uncleanness and offering ineligibility as the stated category, without replacing it only with physical blemish.
verses.before: If it is any unclean animal that may not be presented as an offering to the LORD, the animal will be set before the priest.
verses.after: If it is an unclean animal that may not be offered to the LORD, bring the animal before the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: If it is any unclean animal that may not be presented as an offering to the LORD, the animal shall be set before the priest.

verses.rationale: Preserves good/bad assessment and the binding force of the priest’s valuation rather than leaving the amount to the owner.
verses.before: The priest will assign its value, whether good or bad. Whatever valuation the priest assigns, so it will be.
verses.after: The priest is to assess its value, whether good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets will stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall assign its value, whether good or bad. Whatever valuation the priest assigns, so it shall be.

verses.rationale: Clarifies redeeming actor and animal while retaining the exact added fraction.
verses.before: If the owner wishes to redeem it, one-fifth will be added to its valuation.
verses.after: If the person who made the vow redeems the animal, he must add one-fifth to its assessed value.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the owner wishes to redeem it, one-fifth shall be added to its valuation.

verses.rationale: Retains house consecration, condition-based assessment and the same binding valuation language as verse 12.
verses.before: If someone dedicates a house as holy to the LORD, the priest will assign its value, whether good or bad. Whatever valuation the priest assigns, so it will stand.
verses.after: If someone consecrates his house as holy to the LORD, the priest is to assess it, whether good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets will stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone dedicates a house as holy to the LORD, the priest shall assign its value, whether good or bad. Whatever valuation the priest assigns, so it shall stand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the original dedicator’s redemption, silver amount, added fifth and restored possession.
verses.before: If the one who dedicated the house wishes to redeem it, that person will add one-fifth to the valuation price, and the house will again belong to that person.
verses.after: If the person who consecrated the house redeems it, he must add one-fifth of its assessed value in silver. Then the house will belong to him again.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the one who dedicated the house wishes to redeem it, that person shall add one-fifth to the valuation price, and the house shall again belong to that person.

verses.rationale: Makes seed capacity the field-assessment basis; retains barley, homer and fifty shekels without importing modern land area or crop yield.
verses.before: If someone dedicates to the LORD part of a field from ancestral possession, the valuation will be according to the amount of seed required for it: a homer of barley seed will be valued at fifty shekels of silver.
verses.after: If someone consecrates part of his family’s field to the LORD, assess it according to the seed needed to sow it: fifty shekels of silver for land sown with a homer of barley seed.
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone dedicates to the LORD part of a field from ancestral possession, the valuation shall be according to the amount of seed required for it: a homer of barley seed shall be valued at fifty shekels of silver.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the Jubilee-year valuation as the starting amount before later reductions, retaining stand as validity.
verses.before: If the field is dedicated beginning in the Year of Jubilee, the full valuation will stand.
verses.after: If he consecrates his field in the Jubilee year, the full assessed value will stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the field is dedicated beginning in the Year of Jubilee, the full valuation shall stand.

verses.rationale: Preserves remaining-year calculation and deduction rather than charging the whole cycle’s price after part has elapsed.
verses.before: But if the field is dedicated after the Jubilee, the priest will calculate the price according to the years remaining until the Year of Jubilee, and the valuation will be reduced accordingly.
verses.after: If he consecrates it after the Jubilee, the priest is to calculate the amount according to the years left until the next Jubilee year and reduce the assessed value accordingly.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the field is dedicated after the Jubilee, the priest shall calculate the price according to the years remaining until the Year of Jubilee, and the valuation shall be reduced accordingly.

verses.rationale: Keeps the same dedicator, added fifth, silver and return as the house rule without losing the field referent.
verses.before: If the one who dedicated the field wishes to redeem it, that person will add one-fifth to the valuation price, and it will remain theirs.
verses.after: If the person who consecrated the field redeems it, he must add one-fifth of its assessed value in silver. Then the field will belong to him again.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the one who dedicated the field wishes to redeem it, that person shall add one-fifth to the valuation price, and it shall remain theirs.

verses.rationale: Uses a passive for the disputed seller while retaining nonredemption, sale and permanent loss of redemption; note preserves alternative subjects and logical connection.
verses.before: But if that person does not redeem the field, or if the field has been sold to another person, it may no longer be redeemed.
verses.after: If he does not redeem the field and it is sold to someone else, it can no longer be redeemed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if that person does not redeem the field, or if the field has been sold to another person, it may no longer be redeemed.

verses.rationale: Keeps Jubilee release distinct from return to the original family and introduces herem’s irrevocable category with the priest as recipient.
verses.before: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will be holy to the LORD like a field devoted to the LORD; it will become the priest’s possession.
verses.after: When the field is released at the Jubilee, it will be holy to the LORD, like a field devoted beyond recall. It will become the priest’s holding.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it shall be holy to the LORD like a field devoted to the LORD; it shall become the priest’s possession.

verses.rationale: Retains the purchased-versus-inherited distinction and lets the condition continue into the priest’s calculation.
verses.before: If someone dedicates to the LORD a field that was purchased and is not part of ancestral possession,
verses.after: If someone consecrates to the LORD a field he bought, one that is not part of his family holding,
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone dedicates to the LORD a field that was purchased and is not part of ancestral possession,

verses.rationale: Keeps that-day payment as written rather than silently adding Jubilee before day; distinguishes payment timing from the valuation endpoint.
verses.before: the priest will calculate for that person the amount of the valuation up to the Year of Jubilee, and the person will give the valuation on that day as something holy to the LORD.
verses.after: the priest is to calculate its assessed value for the years until the Jubilee. The man is to pay that amount that very day as something holy to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: the priest shall calculate for that person the amount of the valuation up to the Year of Jubilee, and the person shall give the valuation on that day as something holy to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Clarifies original holder and purchaser so consecration does not erase the prior family’s land right.
verses.before: In the Year of Jubilee the field will return to the person from whom it was bought, the one whose ancestral possession of the land it was.
verses.after: In the Jubilee year, the field returns to the person he bought it from, the one whose family holding the land is.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to the person from whom it was bought, the one whose ancestral possession of the land it was.

verses.rationale: Preserves the universal valuation standard and exact twenty-gerah equivalence without monetary modernization.
verses.before: Every valuation will be according to the sanctuary shekel: twenty gerahs will make one shekel.
verses.after: Every assessment must use the sanctuary shekel. A shekel is twenty gerahs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every valuation shall be according to the sanctuary shekel: twenty gerahs shall make one shekel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the already-due restriction and renders seh with sheep and goats instead of excluding goats from the category.
verses.before: But no one may dedicate the firstborn of an animal, because as firstborn it already belongs to the LORD. Whether ox or sheep, it belongs to the LORD.
verses.after: No one may consecrate a firstborn animal that already belongs to the LORD as a firstborn. Whether from cattle, sheep or goats, it belongs to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: But no one may dedicate the firstborn of an animal, because as firstborn it already belongs to the LORD. Whether ox or sheep, it belongs to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains ransom and redeem verbs, extra fifth only for redemption, and sale at assessed value; note leaves the unclean animal’s connection to firstborn open.
verses.before: If it is an unclean animal, the owner may redeem it according to the valuation and will add one-fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it will be sold according to the valuation.
verses.after: If it is an unclean animal, its owner may ransom it at the assessed value plus one-fifth. If it is not redeemed, it is to be sold at the assessed value.
verses.tsw_comparator: If it is an unclean animal, the owner may redeem it according to the valuation and shall add one-fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it shall be sold according to the valuation.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three categories including people, both prohibitions and most-holy status; herem is distinguished from an ordinary redeemable vow.
verses.before: But nothing that someone devotes irrevocably to the LORD from anything they possess—whether a human being, an animal, or an ancestral field—may be sold or redeemed. Everything devoted irrevocably is most holy to the LORD.
verses.after: But anything someone devotes beyond recall to the LORD from what belongs to him—whether a person, an animal or part of his family’s field—must neither be sold nor redeemed. Everything devoted beyond recall is most holy to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: But nothing that someone devotes irrevocably to the LORD from anything they possess—whether a human being, an animal, or an ancestral field—may be sold or redeemed. Everything devoted irrevocably is most holy to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit human death penalty and nonransomability without inventing a limitation to war prisoners or implying every ordinary vow is lethal.
verses.before: No human being devoted to destruction may be ransomed; that person will surely be put to death.
verses.after: No person placed under such a ban may be ransomed. That person must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: No human being devoted to destruction may be ransomed; that person shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Retains tithe, both produce categories and repeated belonging/holiness relationship.
verses.before: Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
verses.after: Every tithe from the land, whether from its grain or the fruit of its trees, belongs to the LORD. It is holy to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves partial redemption and the added fifth; value clarifies the monetary calculation without changing the proportion.
verses.before: If someone wishes to redeem any of the tithe, one-fifth will be added to it.
verses.after: If someone redeems any of his tithe, he must add one-fifth to its value.
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone wishes to redeem any of the tithe, one-fifth shall be added to it.

verses.rationale: Retains the actual tenth-animal procedure and rod image, with flock including sheep and goats rather than sheep alone.
verses.before: Every tithe of herd or flock—every tenth animal that passes under the staff—will be holy to the LORD.
verses.after: For the tithe of cattle, sheep and goats, every tenth animal that passes under the rod is holy to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every tithe of herd or flock—every tenth animal that passes under the staff—shall be holy to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prohibition of selecting by quality and exchanging, and applies holy/nonredeemable status to both animals.
verses.before: The owner will not examine whether it is good or bad and will not exchange it. If it is exchanged, both it and its substitute will be holy; it may not be redeemed.”
verses.after: Do not pick out good animals from bad or make a substitution. If an animal is exchanged, both it and its substitute become holy and may not be redeemed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The owner shall not examine whether it is good or bad and shall not exchange it. If it is exchanged, both it and its substitute shall be holy; it may not be redeemed.”

verses.rationale: Retains the closing command summary, Moses, Israel and Sinai without merging it with 26:46.
verses.before: These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
verses.after: These are the commandments the LORD gave Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
